In the club handicap events the results were as under:— 100 yards.—1, J.
Junior handicap we only had one heat, and the winner was J. Thomas, who is quite a promising recruit to our sprinting ranks, with Frank Kemp second and Ian Forrester third.
J. Thomas and Ian Forrester were runners-up to Breacker, of Mitcham, in the 100 yards, and Frank Kemp was second in the 220 and appeared unable to negotiate the rather sharp bends at this track.

Ian Badiali won the senior 440 and Bob Taylor was first home in the senior 880, while Alan Sexton, after being second in the senior 100, duly won the senior 220 yards. Bob Wolton won the junior 440 and J.
Wright second in the 440, and J.
Frank Kemp again won the 220 yards junior, with J. Thomas second and Alan Law third, while Alan Sexton regained the senior 220 title, with Frank Craft second and Basil Walden third.

During the 1920's Belgravian J.N.Thomas, who began his race walking at the age of 44 with North London Harriers, became the first walker in history to finish three successive Brighton and Back races.
Between 1921 and 1929 J.N. Thomas became the first walker in history to successfully complete three successive London to Brighton and Back Walks (104 miles).
